confluence.error.disabled: Publishing to Confluence is off: set confluence.enabled=true
confluence.error.matplotlib: Publishing charts to Confluence needs the matplotlib package. Install it: pip install matplotlib
confluence.forecast.after_scaling: After that, CPU is enough up to {rps}; beyond it, {service} hits the limit first.
confluence.forecast.busiest: Busiest: {name}, pod CPU at the target ≈ {cpu}, ceiling {ceiling}.
confluence.forecast.caption_instability: Green zone: load with headroom; yellow: no headroom; red: stalls began at this load in the test. Hatching: above the tested load, calculation only.
confluence.forecast.caption_model: Green zone: load with headroom; yellow: no headroom; red: above the model ceiling. Hatching: above the tested load, calculation only.
confluence.forecast.caption_no_limit: Green bar: the load the test passed without stalls; hatching: above the tested load, calculation only.
confluence.forecast.caption_sla: Green zone: load with headroom; yellow: no headroom; red: above the report maximum, where the test broke the SLA thresholds. Hatching: above the tested load, calculation only.
confluence.forecast.cause_instability: Stalls from {rps} are explained by CPU: {service} at this load ≈ {cpu} per pod.
confluence.forecast.cause_model: The model ceiling of {rps} is explained by CPU: {service} at this load ≈ {cpu} per pod.
confluence.forecast.cause_sla: The SLA breach from {rps} is explained by CPU: {service} at this load ≈ {cpu} per pod.
confluence.forecast.check_unverified: numbers not found in the data: {numbers}
confluence.forecast.check_verified: numbers checked against the data: {matched} of {total}
confluence.forecast.limit_instability: Limit {rps}: stalls began at this load in the test.
confluence.forecast.limit_model: Limit {rps}: the throughput ceiling of the model.
confluence.forecast.limit_none: The data shows no limit: RPS grows almost linearly across the tested range.
confluence.forecast.limit_not_cpu: The {rps} limit is not related to service CPU: adding pods will not remove it.
confluence.forecast.limit_sla: Limit {rps}: the report shows the SLA thresholds broken from this load.
confluence.forecast.limit_sla_checks: Limit {rps}: the report shows the SLA thresholds broken from this load ({checks}).
confluence.forecast.method_cpu: The CPU line is fitted to {count} steps without stalls.
confluence.forecast.method_excluded: Left out of the model: load ramp-up and ramp-down ({edges}), stalls ({stalls}).
confluence.forecast.method_excluded_degr: Left out of the model: points above the report maximum, where the SLA thresholds broke ({count}).
confluence.forecast.method_pods: Pods: pod CPU = base + cost × RPS per pod, a straight line over the stable steps of each service. Pods needed = cost × target / (ceiling − base). The load is split evenly between pods, with the request mix of the test.
confluence.forecast.method_usl: USL model over {count} points of {minutes} min; R² = {r2}.
confluence.forecast.method_usl_ceiling: USL model over {count} points of {minutes} min, model ceiling {rps}; R² = {r2}.
confluence.forecast.no_related: {reason} The report has no related findings.
confluence.forecast.no_target: No target is set: enter the target load on the forecast page and publish again.
confluence.forecast.no_verdict: The forecast for the “{title}” scenario ({rps} RPS) gave no verdict
confluence.forecast.nothing_to_explain: The data shows no limit, so there is nothing to analyse.
confluence.forecast.params: target {target}, pod CPU ceiling {ceiling}, headroom to the limit {headroom}
confluence.forecast.safe_cpu: Safe maximum of the current configuration: {rps}; beyond it, {service} goes above the pod CPU ceiling.
confluence.forecast.safe_headroom: Safe maximum with {headroom} headroom to the limit: {rps}.
confluence.forecast.scenario_blocked: pods will not help: the {rps} limit is not related to CPU
confluence.forecast.section_scale: Where the target sits on the load scale
confluence.forecast.stale: the analysis is out of date: refresh it on the forecast page
confluence.forecast.stuck: {name}: pod CPU at zero load ≈ {cpu} is above the ceiling; pods will not help
confluence.forecast.tight: Headroom to the limit is {headroom}, {required} required.
confluence.judge.label_grounding: Conclusions tied to metrics and series
confluence.judge.note: The data check is heuristic: it rates how the text is tied to metrics, whether the numbers match and whether peak_performance is consistent.
confluence.judge.numeric: Numbers in the text that match
confluence.judge.numeric_none: not checked, the findings have no explicit numeric claims
confluence.judge.skipped: did not run: the model gave a single answer
confluence.judge.title: Answer assessment
confluence.sla.empty: No SLA criteria are set for this service, so the automatic verdict is “{verdict}”.
confluence.sla.mean_note: The RPS in the step table is the mean of the whole interval; the thresholds are checked on this window.
confluence.sla.stable_step_level: SLA checked on a stable step, window RPS {level}
confluence.sla.stable_step_span: SLA checked on a stable step, window {window}
confluence.sla.stable_step_span_level: SLA checked on a stable step, window {window}, window RPS {level}
confluence.sla.step_level: SLA checked on step {index} ({interval}), window RPS {level}
confluence.steps.note: RPS is the step level. Response time is the p95 on the plateau, without the tail after a drop.
confluence.template.placeholder_missing: Placeholder {placeholder} is not on Confluence page {page}
confluence.verdict.title: Verdict
